It’s an ordinary afternoon. Ordinary as canyoneering the trails on a familiar trail in this familiar town, but something has shifted inside my bones and now my feet feel different than the way they’ve traveled for so damn-long here.
There was the sound and sight, of rustle, the smell like wet soil that was so fresh it could still hold the rain from a day or a night prior to now and there are always birds singing and leaves rustled with wind. There is no change.
There is the sound as always of crunches as I traverse my old, familiar ground with the familiar, old worn boots I have had these boots since the time they gave them as an adult birthday. But the sound has never changed and that's what is now familiar, the change of that sound and my old, trusted shoes that I can now walk the trail on with my own bare foot. I feel it and the earth beneath me feels new and alive in ways that never before did as I stepped bare.
